subject.title: Feature Request: Add parseMode config for Telegram channels

question: Which Telegram formatting modes should OpenClaw publicly support, and should account-level settings override the channel default across text, rich messages, captions, edits, and draft previews?
rationale: This establishes a compatibility-sensitive public configuration and escaping contract; source-level wiring cannot safely choose the permanent policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve a conservative selector
options.body: Support a documented safe default plus an explicit plain-text mode, with one account-over-channel precedence rule and no raw-markup bypass.

options.title: Approve broader formatting modes
options.body: Also support MarkdownV2 and/or HTML, after specifying escaping, entity handling, rich-message interaction, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Defer the selector
options.body: Keep the current formatting contract and track specific rich-message, spacing, or custom-emoji regressions as narrower work.

recommendation.title: Approve a conservative selector
recommendation.body: Support a documented safe default plus an explicit plain-text mode, with one account-over-channel precedence rule and no raw-markup bypass.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history links this contributor to the current Telegram formatting direction and adjacent configuration work.
